On Tue, Nov 2, 2027 at 09:24, laura_bennett@redwood.com wrote:
> Immediate ask: Hannah & Marcus, can you triage routing and LB health? If this is a queue-amplification effect we should consider aggressive 502 protection (early drop) and enable fallback routing for critical checkout paths.

Taking point on LB side. Current findings:
- USW LB backlog metric jumped from baseline ~30ms to 1.8s; worker pools for the model-serving tier report thread saturation and connection queue growth.
- We observed a small set of clients that retried aggressively (exponential backoff not honored). That produced request bursts that pushed service CPU to queue incoming requests.

Immediate mitigation applied (10:05 UTC):
1) Enabled staged early-drop (503) for non-critical routes to reduce head-of-line blocking.
2) Throttled problematic client IP ranges at the LB.
3) Opened routing fallback to a lower-capacity EU pool for read-only inference paths (non-payment) to reduce pressure on USW.

Next actions: Marcus to increase worker pool in USW (hot-add) and validate KV cache warmup. Laura — please prep a short customer note; Evelyn will help with executive summary.

- Hannah
SRE Lead, Edge Operations

Updating with capacity work and observations.
- Hot-add of +4 worker instances to the USW pool completed at 11:03 UTC; CPU and queueing metrics improved but latency still above SLO for the checkout route.
- Found repeated client connection resets from a subset of Brightfield SDK hosts; their retry policy was set to fixed interval 200ms x 5 which amplified load. We engaged their SDK team to request immediate backoff change.
- Deployed a temporary KV cache priming task (11:10 UTC) to reduce cold-start tokenization cost for the busiest models.

Action items I own:
1) Monitor error rate and revert early-drop once 5xx < 1% for 15m.
2) Prepare a short rollback checklist for hot-addted workers.

Marcus Lin

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Production: spike of 502/503 responses + client retries (USW) — customer note and exec summary

Hi Sylvia / Brightfield team — thank you for the rapid signal and logs. Short update and next steps:

What happened
- A subset of Brightfield client instances retried aggressively during a transient latency increase in our USW edge, producing a request surge that amplified queueing and resulted in elevated 502/503s. A spillover effect led to higher 429s in an EU service pool for read-only inference paths.

What we did (timeline highlights)
- 10:05 UTC: early-drop configuration for low-priority routes; targeted IP throttles applied.
- 11:03 UTC: hot-add +4 serving workers; KV priming task; opened fallback routing for non-payment traffic.
- 11:30–12:00 UTC: error rate dropped from peak ~18% 5xx to ~1.4%; continued to monitor.

Customer impact
- Checkout errors peaked for ~18 minutes; recovery visible within ~90 minutes of first signal. No data loss; transient latency impacted user conversions.

Next steps (collaborative)
- Brightfield: adjust SDK retry policy (recommend exponential backoff with jitter, starting at 200ms, max 2s, max attempts 3).
- Redwood: introduce a more conservative early-drop policy for checkout-critical routes and add a circuit-breaker to isolate noisy clients sooner.
- Joint: post-incident review next week; we will share metrics and a short runbook update.

Attachments: proposed_fallback_plan_v1.pdf

Evelyn Hart
VP, Customer Success & Operations
Redwood Inference
